name: Tema
overview: Tema is identified as a male figure mentioned uniquely in Rahlfs' Septuaginta translation of Genesis 25:3 as a son of Jokshan. There is no tribal affiliation or surname attributed to him in the biblical text. Notably, the name Tema does not appear in the traditional Hebrew Masoretic Text but is present in this Greek manuscript tradition.
namesAndTitles: The name Tema appears once in the biblical record, specifically in Genesis 25:3 as preserved in the Septuaginta. There is no provided meaning or divine origin attached to the name, and it is used simply as a proper name without additional titles or significance.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture records Tema as a son of Jokshan, but no other family relationships or connections are documented. Beyond this paternal link, the biblical text does not provide further information about his family or descendants.
scriptureSignificance: Tema's mention as a son of Jokshan situates him within the genealogical framework of Genesis, contributing to the broader understanding of Abraham's lineage. The presence of his name in the Septuaginta but absence in the Masoretic Text highlights variations in manuscript traditions. While not elaborated upon in the biblical narrative, his inclusion reflects the detailed genealogical records important for tracing the origins of peoples in Scripture.
